subject.title: Codex turn fails with generic Telegram fallback when invalid image tool model is configured, leaving child agent orphaned on full stdout pipe

question: Should OpenClaw fail invalid explicit image-generation model refs at config/startup time, or keep runtime resolution while improving Telegram diagnostics and cleanup?
rationale: The remaining work crosses config compatibility, provider/model routing, Telegram user-facing diagnostics, and Codex lifecycle ownership; an automated fix could choose the wrong boundary or break existing provider setups.

options.title: Runtime diagnostics plus cleanup proof
options.body: Keep current runtime model resolution, but surface actionable Telegram errors with an error id/log pointer and prove parent-failure subprocess cleanup.

options.title: Strict config preflight
options.body: Reject unknown explicit image-generation model refs during config validation and add any needed doctor or upgrade guidance for existing configs.

options.title: Split into canonical follow-ups
options.body: Keep this issue as the diagnostics/process-lifecycle tracker and open a narrower config-validation item for the model-ref policy decision.

recommendation.title: Runtime diagnostics plus cleanup proof
recommendation.body: Keep current runtime model resolution, but surface actionable Telegram errors with an error id/log pointer and prove parent-failure subprocess cleanup.

likelyOwner.reason: This account appears across the Codex app-server, model catalog, and image-generation routing history most central to choosing the owner boundary.
